method.rdap: Only anonymous HTTPS GET to Verisign /com|net/v1/domain/{registry-domain}; public pinned service IP, TLS verified, no redirect or credentials, response <=128 KiB, hard process deadline 11 s.
method.doh: Only anonymous A/AAAA RFC8484 requests to dns.alidns.com and doh.pub; public pinned resolver IP, TLS verified, no redirects; response <=64 KiB, hard process deadline 11 s.
method.pace: Two rounds, at most two concurrent worker processes, at least 0.4 s between starts; no retries.
method.controls: In each round use google.com/google.net and randomized synthetic negative .com/.net for RDAP and each DoH provider; candidate requests run only if the corresponding .com control succeeds.

method_precision: Concurrency and interval refer to worker process starts; actual network requests may start closer together due to independent setup and DNS resolution.
No retry was scheduled. Failed per-TLD/provider controls suppress the corresponding candidate requests; skipped queries are recorded separately.
Hard process deadline includes service DNS, connection, TLS, request, and bounded response read.
limitations: No registry body, registration or registrant details, concrete address, CNAME, DNS answer or user data retained. RDAP body and DNS hashes cannot reconstruct omitted responses.
Queries are to service providers only; source pages, rules and source-host IP connections are never accessed.
All observations share a network path and are close in time; recursive resolver negative caching means they are not independent geographic or temporal proof.
NXDOMAIN and RDAP 404 are point-in-time evidence, not proof of ownership, business closure, malware, source failure or permanent availability.
The root is a syntactic second-level .com/.net zone and may host unrelated services. A matching registry object does not imply a source works.
The 18 domains refer to selected bundled records, not verified user installations or settings.
The collection scripts and draft were local build artifacts and were not added to the repository; re-running a new collector cannot reproduce prior responses.
Sibling HTTP statuses are transport observations, not proof of ownership, successful reading, or safety.
One bundled endpoint contains a query; raw endpoints and URL queries are not included here. The historical source identity can be checked against the archive offline.
